title: Mission APIMpossible - allowlisted Responses request
description: A deliberately narrow subset of the Azure OpenAI v1 Responses request. This is an enterprise allowlist, not a pass-through proxy: anything not named here is rejected. Adding a field requires a documented threat model. See docs/security.md.

model.description: Must equal the single approved deployment name. APIM re-checks this against the configured allowlist; schema validation alone is not the control.

input.description: Either a single text prompt or a bounded, text-only message history maintained by the client. Text only: no file, image or audio parts, and no URL-bearing structures.

oneOf.comment: Inlined deliberately. A '#/definitions/...' $ref is resolved relative to the DOCUMENT root, and APIM stores this schema nested under components.schemas, so the pointer would not resolve at runtime and the array form would silently fail open.

items.comment: Three item shapes. A text turn is the original contract - and it accepts BOTH a plain string and the canonical array of typed parts, because a real IDE sends the latter: GitHub Copilot was measured sending content as [{type:input_text,text:...}] with an item-level type of 'message'. The two function_call shapes exist ONLY so a CLIENT-SIDE tool loop can replay its own prior turns: the model asks, the CLIENT executes on its own machine, and the client sends the result back. The service never executes anything.

oneOf.comment: A text turn, in either the plain or canonical form.

type.comment: Present on canonical items. Only 'message' is accepted here; the function_call shapes are separate branches.

id.comment: Opaque item identifier echoed by some clients. Bounded, never interpreted.

oneOf.comment: The canonical form. Text parts ONLY - input_image, input_file and input_audio are absent by design, so an attachment is rejected rather than silently dropped.
A tool call the model previously requested, replayed by the client.

arguments.comment: A JSON string produced by the model. Bounded, and never parsed or executed by the gateway.

oneOf.comment: The result the CLIENT produced by running that tool locally.

instructions.description: System-style guidance applied to this single stateless request.

stream.description: Server-sent events. APIM forwards the stream without buffering.

store.description: Must be literal boolean false when present. APIM rejects true and injects false when the field is omitted, so no response is persisted server-side. This governs Responses storage; it is not a claim that all service-side abuse-monitoring retention is disabled.

max_output_tokens.description: Bounded output. The deployed model may impose a lower ceiling.

temperature.description: Only forwarded when the approved model supports it. Reasoning models reject this field; the client should omit it.

reasoning.description: Reasoning controls only. Encrypted reasoning items are deliberately not enabled in the initial contract; enabling them requires an explicit feature review.

tools.description: CLIENT-SIDE function tools only. The model may ask for one to be called; the caller decides whether to run it, runs it on its own machine, and sends the result back. The service executes nothing. 'type' is const 'function' precisely so hosted tools - code_interpreter, file_search, mcp, computer_use, web_search - cannot be named here: those move execution server-side, which is the property this contract exists to protect.

name.comment: 128 chars. Measured longest from a real VS Code tool catalogue: 56 ('activate_fallback_mcp_pylance_mcp_s_pylancePythonDebug_1'). MCP-namespaced names concatenate server and tool identifiers, so they grow with nesting depth. Dots are permitted because MCP naming commonly uses them; the value is an opaque identifier that is never used as a path or an expression.

description.comment: 32 KiB. This was 4096 and it was the single reason every GitHub Copilot agent request was rejected: the run_in_terminal tool alone ships a 5,859-character description. Tool descriptions are prompt engineering, not labels, and they get long. The bound exists to stop an unbounded field, not to second-guess a client's prompt.

parameters.description: A JSON Schema for the tool's arguments, passed through as an opaque object. The gateway does not interpret it.

tool_choice.description: How the model should select among the client-side tools above.

name.comment: Must match the bound on tools[].name, or a caller could name a tool it is not allowed to declare.

truncation.description: How the service should handle a context window overflow. 'auto' lets it drop middle-of-conversation items; 'disabled' fails instead. Bounded to those two values. This governs transient request handling, not persistence: it does not store anything, and store=false still applies. GitHub Copilot sends this on every agent-mode request.

parallel_tool_calls.description: Whether the model may request several client-side tools at once. Execution still happens on the caller's machine either way.

metadata.description: Caller-supplied labels. Never used for authorization and never treated as identity.
